findings.title: Org/team raw SQL conditions are never executed against the database
findings.body: The only actual database execution in this suite is the simple user-scope query. The org and team authorization paths generate array predicates and top-level OR conditions, but the tests only compare Prisma.sql fragment objects. That does not prove the generated SQL is valid or returns the correct rows. Add integration tests that execute getBaseConditions for team and org scopes against seeded bookings that should be included and excluded.

findings.title: Public service API changed from findMany/Prisma where inputs to raw SQL fragments
findings.body: The previous public findMany method is removed, and authorization/filter helpers now return Prisma.Sql instead of Prisma where input objects. Any existing consumer of InsightsBookingService will break unless updated. If this service is used elsewhere, callers need to be migrated in this change or a compatible query API should be preserved.

findings.title: Org scope skips org-member individual bookings when the org has no child teams
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition always includes the org id in teamIds, but it only fetches membership user IDs when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. For an organization with no child teams, userIdsFromOrg becomes empty, so individual bookings from org members are excluded. If at least one child team exists, org memberships are included. This makes org-scope visibility inconsistent. Query memberships for the org id and child team ids unconditionally.

findings.title: getBaseConditions can return an unwrapped top-level OR fragment
findings.body: When there are no filter conditions, getBaseConditions returns authConditions directly. For org/team scopes this may be a top-level OR expression. If a caller composes the returned fragment with additional AND predicates, SQL operator precedence can change the meaning of the query. Return a parenthesized fragment or clearly document that the result must only be used as a complete WHERE clause.

findings.title: Membership lookups do not use the injected Prisma client
findings.body: The service receives a Prisma client and uses it for TeamRepository, but membership checks call static MembershipRepository methods without passing the injected client. If those static methods use a global/default client, authorization checks may run on a different connection, transaction, or read replica than the rest of the service. Pass the injected client to membership repository calls or confirm the static methods intentionally use the same client.
